title: DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation
hook: DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation shows up in everyday JavaScript and in senior interviews — this page explains what it is, why it matters, and how it behaves in the engine versus C# or TypeScript.

blocks.text: DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation is a core concept in JavaScript (ECMAScript). At run time, the engine enforces behavior dynamically — there is no compile step unless you add TypeScript on top. This page explains the idea in plain English first, then shows small, explained examples you can run in the browser console or Node.js.

blocks.text: Senior interviews and production code both probe whether you understand DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation beyond syntax memorization. Misunderstanding here leads to subtle bugs — wrong equality results, leaked memory, untyped JSON boundaries, or async ordering surprises. If you know C#, the comparison sections below help you transfer mental models instead of starting from zero.

blocks.title: Interview trap
blocks.body: Interviewers often ask "DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation" as a follow-up to a coding exercise. They want mechanism and tradeoffs — not a one-line definition.

Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Treating DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation as pure syntax without run-time behavior. Skipping validation at JSON or API boundaries. Saying "it works on my machine" without noting browser versus Node differences.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: add logging or DevTools breakpoints around DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation, write a failing test that captures the edge case, and explain tradeoffs aloud in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the engine does — plus when not to use the clever version.
